header.provenance: own-binary-via-Ghidra (function entry points + RTTI vtable map) + objdump -d -M intel over .text of the same sha256-pinned file
header.status: LEADS, NOT FACTS. Every row carries the instruction address that produced it. Per project rule a number enters a layout header or the manifest only after that instruction has been read back and cited in the header itself. Nothing here is a confirmed fact.
header.what_this_is: Constructor-mined member offsets: every [receiver+disp] store inside a constructor body, with the width of the store and the instruction address that proves it.
the_trap_and_the_defence: UnitClass::TryToDeploy writes [EBX+0x6CA] where EBX is the BuildingClass being deployed, not the unit -- the same body reads [EBX+0x520] as a type pointer. A sweep over a class's methods invents members that do not exist.

Defence 1: constructors only. A candidate is a function that stores a known RTTI vtable through its receiver, or that is called on the pointer returned by operator new. Arbitrary methods are never mined.

Defence 2: a forward dataflow from the entry tracks which registers and ebp-relative frame slots still provably hold the entry ECX. MOV ESI,ECX propagates it; a reload of ESI from anywhere else, a partial-register write, a POP, or a CALL (for the volatile EAX/ECX/EDX) drops it. Only stores through a location still in that set are recorded. Paths are merged by INTERSECTION at join points, so an offset survives only if the register holds the receiver on every path that reaches it.

Known-rejected examples this reproduces: BulletClass +0xE4 (the only [reg+0xE4] in BulletClass code is off a virtual-call result, and the ctor never writes it) and CellClass +0x14C (past sizeof 0x148) are both absent from this file.

field_notes.kinds: store = a plain move into the member; rmw = a read-modify-write (and/or/xor/add/...), which usually means a bitfield; vptr = a 32-bit immediate in .rdata/.data range, i.e. a vtable pointer; lea = the receiver-relative address was TAKEN, not written -- it proves a sub-object or array starts there (a base ctor call, or the EDI of a REP STOS run).
field_notes.width: bytes moved by the widest store seen at that offset; 0 for a lea-only offset, where the width is unknown.
field_notes.proofs: up to four instruction addresses, each of which can be read back with `ghidra disasm` to confirm the row.
field_notes.class: null when the constructor stores no vtable at offset 0 (a non-polymorphic class, or a sub-object constructor); the offsets are still receiver-tracked and still good leads.
